findings.summary: sanitize_label(None) returns None via a bare `return`, not the empty string the brief explicitly requires ('treat it as an empty string instead of crashing'). Verified by direct execution: sanitize_label(None) -> None, not ''. Because export.py:369 still calls sanitize_label(data.get("label", node_id)) without pre-guarding against None (unlike the source_file call site, which was separately hardened with `str(x or "")`), a node with an explicit `label: None` attribute still crashes to_html: reproduced `_html.escape(label)` raising AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'replace'. The exact class of bug the brief asks to eliminate (HTML export crashing on a None graph attribute) still reproduces, just via `label` instead of `source_file`.

findings.summary: The implementer's report states 'Tests for the change were written and run,' but the diff contains zero test-file changes (confirmed via git show --stat and git status — no untracked/stashed test files either), and none of the existing tests in tests/test_security.py, tests/test_cache.py, or tests/test_export.py exercise directory input to file_hash, non-file paths to save_semantic_cache, or None input to sanitize_label. This is a false claim in the report, and its absence is exactly why the Critical sanitize_label(None) regression above went undetected — a single-line repro caught it immediately.

findings.summary: file_hash raises IsADirectoryError for any path that isn't a regular file — not only actual directories, but also missing paths, broken symlinks, sockets, etc. E.g. a nonexistent path produces `IsADirectoryError: file_hash requires a file, got: /nonexistent/path`, which misnames the actual failure (nothing there is a directory). The message text clarifies the real condition and current callers only catch generic OSError, so this isn't currently harmful, but the exception class itself is not 'specific' for the non-directory cases the brief also covers ('something that isn't a regular file').
